appearance.identity: Slender abandoned tapered concrete lighthouse with surviving cream bands, three narrow stair windows, open lantern frame and rusted shallow cupola.
appearance.epoch: Weathered abandoned exterior in the inspected national tourism photos and credited September 2023 base photograph; no operating lens or glass is invented.
appearance.master: Retain original 13632-triangle master and representative two-degree lean byte-for-byte.
appearance.browser: Authored far levels retain paint ranks, taper, lean, gallery and open lantern. District keeps actual recessed apertures, reduces regular radial subdivisions and repeated rail fittings. Original detailed source supplies street and closeup.
appearance.exclusions: Precise current lean, surveyed azimuth or fine dimensions, operational optics, tide, bathymetry, submerged foundation and exact present shore geometry.

geographic.groundContactBasis: National tourism and inspected photographs show the visible base in the sea. Source Y=0 represents the model waterline placed at the host sea-level plane. It is a visual datum convention, not a measured tide or submerged footing height.
geographic.notes: Photographer GPS and a front-facing door give a reconstructed northwest quadrant only, +/-20 degrees; the exact entrance bearing is not surveyed. The tower lean changes, and -2 degrees is a static representative pose. No tower footprint, submerged footing, bathymetry, current tide or accurate shore outline is claimed. Society 21.8213066 longitude contradicts the national tourism and exact-QID positions and is excluded. +Y up; +Z faces the reconstructed northwest entry/viewpoint direction. Baked representative -2-degree local X lean therefore points northeast; this is not a measured present tilt. National tourism and inspected photographs show the visible base in the sea. Source Y=0 represents the model waterline placed at the host sea-level plane. It is a visual datum convention, not a measured tide or submerged footing height.
